This is a rough model from a photo; check critical dimensions. You can reopen this sketch later from Saved sketches and change its dimensions.
STL / OBJ / GLB: open in viewer, then ⋮ › Export
Camera permission is needed to take a photo

1. Place the part on a plain surface with a different colour (e.g. white paper for a dark part) and take the photo straight on, from as far away as possible and zoomed in a little, so that perspective distortion stays small.
2. Tap on the part: the outline and holes are found automatically. If the shadow is included or a part is missing, use Detection settings.
3. Enter one known dimension with Scale (e.g. overall width). Then tap any edge or hole and type its real size. Straighten makes nearly horizontal / vertical edges exact.
4. Create STEP: plate parts with a thickness, block parts from two views (top + front), shafts and flanges by revolving.
A single photo cannot capture hidden depth, threads, chamfers or inner pockets; the result is a rough model for quick dimensioning, quotes and fixtures. Sketches are saved: you can reopen them later, change dimensions and create the STEP again.
Technical drawings: choose Multi-view, then Technical drawing (PDF, image or photo of the paper). Tap inside the front view, then switch to Top and Side and tap inside those views on the same page. Enter one dimension with Scale; the other views use the same scale. In both ISO E (European) and ISO A (American) drawings the front of the part is at the bottom of the top view, so keep Part front: bottom of image. The view to the right of the front view is seen from the left in ISO E and from the right in ISO A; set Side view accordingly. Only outer outlines and round holes are taken; sections, hidden lines, chamfers and threads are ignored.
